accepted_scope_caveats.label: Open-ended Question 1 and all fiber results
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The recording/transition exclusion S_{t+1} ⟂ M_t | (H_t^F,A_t,R_t) is maintained, and the deployment policy is oracle when it depends on latent rewards.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The field-tier claim is conditional on the stated weak-shadow exclusion, known behavior policy and positivity, compatible observed law, and separately supplied deployment sensing/recovery where needed; these conditions do not assume strict nonrectangularity or its certificate.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited work exists as v1 and describes sharp partial-identification bounds from linear programs under a weak-shadow conditional-independence condition, with possible point identification when predictions are informative.

source_verification_receipts.version: Mathematics of Operations Research 30(2), 2005 version of record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Iyengar's paper exists at the stated venue and pages and proves robust-DP extensions when the ambiguity-measure set has a rectangularity property.

The paper studies finite-horizon MNAR-reward OPE, uses future states as shadow variables and a bridge for conditional reward means, and gives an FQE-style estimator with policies depending on past missingness indicators.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper reduces discrete causal-bounding problems to polynomial programs and supplies automated sharp or certified outer bounds; it does not state the proposed sequential weak-shadow strictness certificate.
The cited paper is a standard finite-horizon MDP OPE reference using behavior-policy data and target-policy evaluation, supporting the ordinary OPE framing but not subsuming the MNAR fiber.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: After producing the two-stage dossier, state the strict global-versus-rectangular endpoint inequality as a sharp partial-identification theorem over the printed relatively open observed-law region, rather than leaving its policy decision consequence only in the consumer prose.

Extend the certificate from one H=2 alphabet to an explicitly defined generic class of H>=2 weak-shadow models, proving that the two-stage obstruction embeds while preserving a nonzero endpoint defect.
Add a computable diagnostic that takes an observed table and policy as input and either returns the strictness sign certificate or reports membership in the exceptional equality locus.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 on the exact two-stage elimination dossier, retaining the accepted conditional scope and treating the static reduction and CAD result as supporting rather than headline contributions.
